newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks rise ahead of Morgan Stanley move.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks rise ahead of Morgan Stanley move.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly higher on Saturday on the eve of Morgan Stanley's plan to include Taiwan in its global indices from September 2, brokers said.

The index ended up 14.78 points or 0.23 percent at 6,324.60. Turnover was a modest T$26.2 billion. Brokers said individual investors -- who account for 90 percent of the market's turnover -- kept to the sidelines ahead of the Morgan Stanley move.
"Despite consecutive net buying by institutions this week, individual investors are worried whether foreign funds will really actively enter," said Eric Liu of National Securities.

Liu noted late buying of some blue chips in the plastics, financial and textile sectors. Formosa Plastics rose T$1.50 to T$59.50, Chinatrust Bank gained T$1 to T$52, and Formosa Chemical Fibre rose 50 cents to T$33.70.
Plastics rose most on expected product price increases, while electronics fell on profit-taking after recent gains.
Brokers expect a firmer trend next week.
"Most analysts so far still expect a gradual upward trend, although foreign funds will not necessarily be active because of the slowing economy," Liu said.
